steps.say: Editing means improving your writing. Proofreading means checking for mistakes.
Read your work aloud. If a sentence sounds wrong, look at it again.
Check one thing at a time: capital letters, then full stops, then spelling.
Make sure verbs agree with their subjects and stay in the same tense.
steps.show: The children were...     Yesterday we visited...

steps.say: Swap dull or repeated words for precise ones.

check.prompt: One word is spelt wrongly. Write it correctly. We will go to the beach tommorow.
hints: Look closely at the double letters in each word.
One word has a double letter in the wrong place.
Say the word slowly in three parts. Which part has a double letter?
check.explanation: Tomorrow has one m and two r letters.

options.text: My sister and I went to the market.
Me and my sister went to the market.
options.why: Me cannot be the subject. Use My sister and I.

options.text: My sister and me went to the market.
My sister and I goes to the market.
options.why: Goes does not agree with My sister and I.

hints: Check who is doing the action.
Try the sentence with only one person: I went or me went?
Then check that the verb agrees with two people.
check.explanation: My sister and I is the subject, and went agrees with it.
